abstract_sentences.text: Electronic health records (EHR) pose large-scale multi-disease modeling problems in which many outcomes are rare and strongly influenced by shared risk factors.

evidence.anchor: many outcomes are rare and strongly influenced by shared risk factors

abstract_sentences.text: While modern approaches achieve strong predictive performance, they often treat diseases independently or rely on black-box architectures, offering limited insight into how risk factors organize disease risk and little principled uncertainty quantification.

evidence.anchor: limited insight and little principled uncertainty quantification

abstract_sentences.text: We introduce a Bayesian hypergraph inference framework that reframes multi-disease modeling around latent, risk-factor-modulated disease pathways.

evidence.anchor: reframes multi-disease modeling around latent pathways

abstract_sentences.text: Risk factors act on hyperedges, latent disease subsets with shared risk patterns, allowing diseases to participate in multiple distinct pathways and enabling interpretable, higher-order structure beyond pairwise associations.

evidence.anchor: Risk factors act on hyperedges

abstract_sentences.text: A repulsion prior encourages parsimonious and identifiable structure, while posterior inference provides calibrated uncertainty over both disease groupings and risk-factor influence.

evidence.anchor: repulsion prior and calibrated uncertainty

abstract_sentences.text: To enable scalable inference on large EHR datasets, we develop a structured variational inference algorithm that preserves logical dependencies among hyperedge existence, disease membership, and pathway-level effects.

evidence.anchor: preserves logical dependencies

abstract_sentences.text: Experiments on simulated data and the UK Biobank demonstrate stable and interpretable disease pathway structure, well-calibrated uncertainty, improved estimation for rare diseases, and competitive predictive performance.

experimental_design.name: Simulation data-generating process
experimental_design.description: Simulation uses V=30 diseases and true E=5 hyperedges; predictor 1 affects multiple hyperedges and remaining predictors affect one each; nonzero effects are drawn from Normal(mu, 0.5 squared), with mu in {1, 1.5, 2}.

experimental_design.name: Simulation repeats and split

result_inventory.claim: BHPI prediction on simulated data is competitive with tuned logistic and stronger than tree and multi-label baselines.
result_inventory.comparison: LGBM 68.50 (0.94) and 69.68 (0.56); Binary Relevance, Classifier Chains, and RAkELd are lower.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Mean (standard deviation) over 50 simulation replicates; AUC multiplied by 100.

evidence.anchor: BHPI achieves predictive performance comparable to optimally tuned logistic regression

result_inventory.claim: BHPI recovers simulated disease effects and latent hypergraph structure.
result_inventory.value: COR(beta, beta-hat)=97.85, H-AUC=96.96, gamma-AUC=97.85; all values are multiplied by 100.
result_inventory.comparison: Optimal logistic coefficient correlation is 95.65; H and gamma recovery are undefined for logistic by construction.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Replicate-level aggregate; no interval or hypothesis test reported.

evidence.anchor: inferred disease-hyperedge incidence matrices closely match the ground truth

result_inventory.claim: The repulsion prior changes latent identifiability metrics more than predictive accuracy.
result_inventory.value: At N=2000, lambda=0 to >0 changes AUC 74.69 to 75.00, Jaccard 0.542 to 0.565, effective edges/RF 1.992 to 1.874, and overlap/RF 0.097 to 0.082.
result_inventory.comparison: Table 7 repeats the direction at N=5000: AUC 74.51 to 74.63 and Jaccard 0.581 to 0.619.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Means in Tables 3 and 7; no significance test for structural metrics.

evidence.anchor: repulsion primarily improves identifiability and interpretability rather than acting as a predictive regularizer
predictive performance remains stable while repulsion reduces redundancy

result_inventory.claim: BHPI has more stable rare-disease discrimination on UKB.
result_inventory.value: Figure 2 shows per-disease delta AUC relative to tuned logistic, stratified by prevalence; no single aggregate number is printed.
result_inventory.comparison: LGBM and Classifier Chains have long lower tails for rare diseases, while BHPI matches or exceeds the baseline in the displayed distributions.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Per-disease delta-AUC distribution over 100 random splits; aggregation denominator and intervals are not stated.

evidence.section: Figure 2 / Predictive Stability in the Rare-Disease Regime

result_inventory.claim: The hypergraph representation has a rare-disease advantage over low-rank and clique alternatives.
result_inventory.value: BHPI mean delta AUC versus logistic is +1.2 for prevalence <2%, +0.2 for 2-5%, and +0.2 for >=5%.
result_inventory.comparison: Paired Wilcoxon p-values are 3e-5, 0.11, and 0.02; BFR and clique-expanded variants do not match the pattern.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Prevalence-stratified mean delta AUC with paired Wilcoxon p-values; correction for multiple comparisons is not described.

evidence.anchor: Only BHPI consistently outperforms optimally tuned logistic regression

result_inventory.claim: High-PIP edges carry the predictive signal and low-PIP edges are near chance.
result_inventory.value: UKB high-PIP-only AUC is 68.7, 69.6, 71.6 versus full 68.9, 69.7, 71.6; simulation high-PIP-only is 75.6 versus full 75.7.
result_inventory.comparison: Low-PIP-only is 58.6, 55.0, 57.4 on UKB and 51.2 on simulation; random subset is higher than low-PIP but below full.
result_inventory.statistical_method: PIP-thresholded masked-model AUC; threshold is PIP > 0.5 and no independent refitting is reported.

evidence.anchor: High-PIP edges retain essentially all predictive signal

result_inventory.claim: UKB posterior structure is sparse, overlapping, and risk-factor selective.
result_inventory.value: With E=60 candidates, posterior expected active hyperedges are 27.2 and 28 have PIP > 0.5; most hyperedges contain 2-12 diseases.
result_inventory.comparison: The figure contrasts localized membership PIPs and selective factor activation with dense latent-factor representations.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Posterior inclusion probabilities and thresholded structural summary; no external structural ground truth.

evidence.anchor: posterior concentrates on a parsimonious solution

result_inventory.claim: Smoking and Dementia examples illustrate divergent and convergent pathway membership.
result_inventory.value: Smoking is shown in respiratory and ulcer pathways; Dementia appears in vascular-cognitive, geriatric frailty, and metabolic-neurodegenerative pathways.
result_inventory.comparison: These are qualitative pathway examples supported by PIPs, edge widths, and cited medical literature.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Qualitative case study; no case-level effect size or causal validation.

evidence.anchor: a single risk factor may influence multiple non-redundant disease pathways
a single disease to participate in multiple pathways

result_inventory.claim: CAVI gives structural PIP calibration and prediction close to full Gibbs MCMC in the reported simulation.
result_inventory.value: CAVI H overlap 0.850 plus or minus 0.054 and AUC 0.741 plus or minus 0.008; ECE values 0.087, 0.028, 0.050.
result_inventory.comparison: MCMC H overlap 0.885 plus or minus 0.068 and AUC 0.747 plus or minus 0.009; ECE values 0.081, 0.058, 0.039.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Mean plus or minus standard deviation over 50 replicates; PIP ECE for H, z, and gamma.

evidence.anchor: CAVI and MCMC achieve comparable PIP calibration

result_inventory.claim: Initialization-aligned structure is stable while exact labeled-edge identifiability is not guaranteed.
result_inventory.value: Initialization overlap is 0.905 plus or minus 0.062 in simulation and 0.875 plus or minus 0.044 on UKB; cross-replicate overlap is 0.81-0.83 and AUC standard deviation is 0.01.
result_inventory.comparison: Remaining differences involve borderline diseases with membership PIPs near 0.5; relabeling-stable quantities are used instead of unique edge labels.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Permutation-aligned overlap and predictive variability; selection uses highest validation performance.

evidence.anchor: exact hyperedge-level identifiability is not guaranteed

result_inventory.claim: The method has a measurable structural-discovery cost but low reported inference latency.
result_inventory.value: UKB E=60 uses 27.8 GB and 73.7 minutes of training with inference below 0.1 ms; simulation runtime rises from 1.6/4.1 seconds at E=10 to 3.2/9.3 seconds at E=20 for N=2000/5000.
result_inventory.comparison: Logistic uses 3.74 GB and 5.82 minutes on UKB with inference below 0.1 ms.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Single reported hardware configurations; runtime table, not a statistical uncertainty estimate.

evidence.anchor: one-time structural discovery tax; inference latency on par with logistic regression

claim_closure.claim: BHPI learns risk-factor-specific, overlapping, higher-order latent disease pathways.
claim_closure.method_response: Latent H, Eq. (2), gamma/mu selectors, and repulsion prior represent factor-modulated hyperedges.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Simulation H/gamma recovery, Figure 3 PIPs, Figure 4 cases, and Table 6 masking support structure-prediction linkage; UKB has no structural ground truth.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 6 restates hyperedges and higher-order organization as the central contribution.

evidence.anchor: disease may be influenced by different features through distinct pathways
sparse, overlapping disease organization and pathway-specific modulation

claim_closure.claim: The repulsion prior yields parsimonious and identifiable non-redundant structure.
claim_closure.method_response: Rrep penalizes overlap among hyperedges activated by the same factor and enters nu, rho, and r updates.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables 3 and 7 and Figures 8-10 show lower redundancy and changed Jaccard/effective-edge metrics; p.19 states permutation symmetry remains.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion says repulsion provides parsimonious and non-redundant pathways.

evidence.anchor: repulsion reduces redundancy and improves stability
repulsion prior reduces redundancy but does not break permutation symmetry

claim_closure.claim: Structured VI preserves existence -> membership -> effect logic and provides calibrated uncertainty.
claim_closure.method_response: Conditional q factors and Eq. (8)-(15) preserve zero constraints and include expected overlap in coordinate updates.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 8 compares CAVI PIP ECE with full Gibbs MCMC; values are similar but not identical and no exact-posterior guarantee is given.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 6 returns to calibrated posterior uncertainty over composition and modulation.

evidence.anchor: conditional factors collapse to Dirac deltas at zero
CAVI and MCMC achieve comparable PIP calibration

claim_closure.claim: Rare-disease risk estimation improves without sacrificing prediction.
claim_closure.method_response: Pathway-level sharing induces disease coefficients from shared hyperedge effects.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 2, Table 4, Table 5, and Table 6 report prevalence-stratified performance, calibration, and masking.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 6 restates stable prediction in the rare-disease regime.

evidence.anchor: advantage strongest for rare diseases

claim_closure.claim: Prediction is competitive with logistic, tree, and multi-label baselines.
claim_closure.method_response: The logistic observation layer is combined with structured pathway sharing.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1 simulation AUC, Table 4 calibration, and Table 5 UKB delta AUC provide the comparisons.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 6 states competitive predictive performance across simulations and UKB.

evidence.anchor: competitive disease risk prediction
competitive predictive calibration across all baselines

claim_closure.claim: Pairwise or clique representations lose hypergraph structural selectivity.
claim_closure.method_response: H retains group membership while clique expansion maps a hyperedge to dense pairwise links.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 5 reports clique density about 65 percent at PIP threshold 0.9 and clique-GCN AUC about 0.50; construction and tuning are not fully detailed.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 6 positions hyperedges as inaccessible to pairwise or independent models.

evidence.anchor: primary advantage is structural selectivity

claim_closure.claim: CAVI scales to biobank-size data with approximately linear per-iteration cost.

claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 10 reports a UKB run with 277,291 participants, 73.7 minutes training, and below 0.1 ms inference.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Scalability is retained as an operational property; future work targets larger genetic features.

final_judgment.single_storyline: The paper recasts multi-disease EHR risk as direct modulation of latent hyperedges by risk factors. Repulsion discourages same-factor redundancy, and structured VI preserves existence -> membership -> effect logic so rare-disease prediction and pathway uncertainty can be reported together.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps the representation choice, logical prior, Algorithm 1, simulation recovery, UKB rare-disease and calibration results, clique comparison, PIP masking, and Smoking/Dementia cases. These objects let a reader separate prediction from structural claims.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A moves the full PG posterior and CAVI algebra; B moves structure visualizations, repulsion/capacity sensitivity, PIP calibration, and initialization; C moves cohort facts, ROC, and extra cases; D moves complexity and runtime. The moves preserve readability but make calibration, identifiability, and compute boundaries cross-reading dependent.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 aligns data, latent hypergraph, factor action, and uncertainty. Tables 3/7 separate prediction from structural ablation; Tables 5/6 connect prevalence and PIP masks to prediction; Figure 4 joins a global graph with readable cases. Eq. (2) plus the logical implications on page 4 gives the shortest mechanism statement.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Identifiable and calibrated are strong early claims. Page 19 limits exact labeled-edge identifiability, and Table 8 shows CAVI differs from MCMC; UKB has no structural truth, no causal test, no misspecification simulation, and incomplete seeds, hyperparameters, and threshold sensitivity.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For latent structures that support both interpretation and prediction, separate component effects on prediction from effects on structural stability and redundancy, add an independent posterior or calibration comparator, and state label symmetry, unavailable real-world truth, and causal scope in the main text.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule applies when the study has a latent object with exchangeable labels or unavailable real-world structural truth. Prediction-only tasks without structural diagnostics need task-specific mechanism tests instead of Jaccard, PIP, or MCMC by default.
